source_claims.statement: Connection reuse often causes false positives for smuggling. Disable reuse first. Use specific probes (HTTP/2 nesting, partial requests, connection-state probe) to distinguish true smuggling, connection-locked, connection-state, and client-side desync.

research_questions.formulation: When a desync proof-of-concept only works with connection reuse, which of the three valid reuse-dependent classes is it, versus pure pipelining false positive?
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: false positive vs real vulnerability class
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that any reuse-dependent behavior is either pure FP or true smuggling

environment_model_updates: Three distinct classes require reuse but have different exploitability

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: disable reuse first, then apply specific probes
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: further impact exploration if a real class is confirmed

negative_inconclusive: Reuse alone is often pure pipelining/keep-alive (false positive)
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat all reuse-dependent findings as false positives
Do not treat them all as classic request smuggling
layer_b_candidate_principles: Always disable connection reuse first when validating desync findings; only then apply class-specific probes
Distinguish connection-locked, connection-state, and client-side desync rather than collapsing them
model_vs_harness: Class distinction is model judgment; automated reuse-disable and probe execution is harness.
